questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, they should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane. All riders should follow this pattern until they have all passed the vehicle.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load loose in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in the sidecar so they do not shift and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place loads toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: On a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should sit:

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle nor in the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the sidecar.
questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam when other vehicles are not nearby, and increase your following distance. Watch the headlights and taillights of vehicles ahead. Their lights help light the road and show you bumps and dips.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is located:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. Use your left foot to operate it. Lift the lever with your foot to shift to a higher gear. Press it down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Both the front and rear brakes.
Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best way to stay close while keeping safe distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close while keeping a safe space cushion. Ride in a single-file line when taking curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A car is entering the highway on a ramp to your right. The driver may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it if needed.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles entering the highway. Move to a lane farther from the ramp if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to enter safely.

questions.question: Which statement about the front brake is true?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is not as powerful as the rear brake.
It is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use when used correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.question: You cannot avoid an object or uneven surface. What should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb some of the impact. Just before hitting it, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Every time you slow down or stop
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you slow down or stop
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When you adjust your mirrors, what should you be able to see?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle
The road in front of your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. A properly adjusted mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but the most important thing is to see the road behind and beside you.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to wobble. What should you do?

options.text: Keep riding. The wobble will fix itself.
Slow down by closing the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by closing the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and downward. Pull off the road as soon as you can and fix the problem causing the wobble.

questions.question: Where should you get main information about your motorcycle?

options.text: From a library book about motorcycles

questions.correctAnswerText: From the owner's manual
questions.explanation: The owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. Read the manual before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: When the rear tire skids, what happens?

options.text: You cannot steer in another direction.
It only matters if the front tire skids too.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot steer in another direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash or injury. Too much brake pressure can lock the rear wheel. Once locked, you lose the ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always stay in it.
Change lane positions often to avoid boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around them.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around them.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position also changes. Pick the position that gives you the most space around you and lets other drivers see you clearly.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, a horn:

options.text: Usually cannot be heard by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can alert someone quickly.
questions.explanation: A horn is a useful tool to alert someone quickly. However, a motorcycle horn is quieter than a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: To lower your crash risk, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Be ready to react to dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you and know what you plan to do. Signal clearly and position your motorcycle well. Keep safe distance around you and watch ahead for dangers.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to ride faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a set location later.
Speed up to match that rider.
Split up and let each rider go at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a set location later.
questions.explanation: If one group member wants to ride faster, let them go ahead. Plan to meet at a spot decided on beforehand.

questions.question: To properly control a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so your arms hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can easily reach all controls. Bend your arms slightly and use them to steer, not to hold yourself up. Press your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced during turns.
